summary.text: A double bond is a covalent bond between two atoms involving four bonding electrons, compared with two in a single bond.
Double bonds occur most commonly between two carbon atoms, as in alkenes, but also join different elements, such as carbon and oxygen in a carbonyl group.
Double bonds involving carbon are stronger and shorter than single bonds, and the atoms cannot rotate around them, which gives rise to cis-trans isomerism.

facts.label: Bonding electrons
facts.value: Four, compared with two in a single bond

facts.label: How it is drawn
facts.value: Two parallel lines, typed as an equals sign

facts.label: Ethylene C=C length
facts.value: 133 pm, versus 154 pm for ethane's C−C

facts.label: Strength
facts.value: 636 versus 368 kJ mol⁻¹ for a single bond

items.prompt: You try to twist one end of an ethylene molecule's carbon-carbon link against the other. Why does it resist?

options.label: The sigma bond is too weak to survive any twisting
The hydrogens on each carbon are too bulky to pass each other
The p-orbitals must stay parallel to overlap, so rotation is not possible
The link is longer than a single bond and so is stiffer

items.explain: For maximum overlap the p-orbitals have to remain parallel, so rotation around the central bond is not possible.

items.prompt: A double bond has two connections between the atoms, yet it is not twice as strong as a single bond. Why not?

options.label: The extra connection, the pi bond, is weaker because its overlap is less effective
The two connections cancel each other out partly
The extra connection only forms when the atoms are far apart
The sigma bond weakens whenever a second connection forms

items.explain: The double bond is stronger than a single bond but not twice as strong, because the pi bond is weaker than the sigma bond due to less effective pi-overlap.

items.prompt: You measure the carbon-carbon distance in ethane and then in ethylene. What do you find?

options.label: Ethylene's is longer, because more electrons crowd between the atoms
The two are the same, since both link carbon to carbon
Ethylene's is shorter, because its sigma bond is the stronger one
Ethylene's is shorter, because its p-orbital overlap is maximised

items.explain: Double bonds are shorter than single bonds because p-orbital overlap is maximized: 133 pm in ethylene versus 154 pm in ethane.

items.prompt: You are scanning compounds for double bonds. Which group of elements is most likely to show them?

options.label: Heavy elements from the lowest rows of the table
Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen from period 2
Elements from every period about equally often
Only carbon, and never any other element

items.explain: Double bonds are common for period 2 elements carbon, nitrogen and oxygen, and less common with higher periods. They also join unlike elements, such as carbon and oxygen.

items.prompt: A molecule alternates double bond, single bond, double bond, single bond along a chain. What can the p-orbital overlap do there?

options.label: Stay locked between just the two atoms of each double bond
Vanish, because single bonds block any overlap
Turn the whole chain into one long triple bond
Extend over several atoms in the chain, forming a conjugated system

items.explain: In molecules with alternating double and single bonds, p-orbital overlap can exist over multiple atoms in a chain, giving a conjugated system.

items.prompt: Alkenes are flat. What shape do double-bonded compounds of the heavier group 14 elements take?

options.label: Twisted or trans bent, not planar
Flat, just like the alkenes
Perfectly straight and linear
Flat, but with much shorter bonds

items.explain: Unlike the alkenes, these compounds are not planar but adopt twisted and/or trans bent structures, and the effect grows for heavier elements.
